title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for persistent joint pain and stiffness.

HPI
The patient is a 52-year-old male presenting today for a follow-up regarding chronic joint pain that has persisted for approximately six months. He reports that the discomfort is most severe in the morning, often lasting for over an hour before he can achieve full range of motion. He describes the sensation as a dull ache that occasionally sharpens with increased activity. He notes that the symptoms are bilateral, affecting his knees and hands equally. He denies any recent trauma to the joints or systemic symptoms such as fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss. He reports that his current management of symptoms has provided modest relief, but he is seeking further evaluation to improve his quality of life and mobility.

Medication List
- Sertraline 50mg daily
- Naproxen 500mg as needed for pain
- Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies any recent fevers or night sweats. He denies any changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency. He denies any new headaches or visual disturbances. He denies any recent skin rashes or itching.

Social History
The patient works as a project manager and reports a sedentary office environment. He exercises by walking three times a week. He denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Father has a history of hypertension and arthritis. Mother has a history of type 2 diabetes.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on room air
Height: 5'11"
Weight: 195 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.6%
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
CRP: 12 mg/L
ESR: 22 mm/hr

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented x3. He appears in no acute distress. Physical examination of the bilateral knees reveals mild swelling and tenderness upon palpation. Range of motion is slightly limited by stiffness. Hand joints show mild swelling at the PIP joints but no significant erythema or warmth. No neurological deficits noted.

Assessment
1. Chronic joint pain and morning stiffness.

Plan
1. Continue current medication list as prescribed.
2. Recommended a referral to physical therapy to focus on strengthening and range of motion.
3. Follow up in 4 weeks to assess progress with therapy.

Electronically signed,
L. Moreau, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: An antidepressant on the list does not establish major depression; coders do not infer diagnoses from medications.

distractors.why: Only the provider can document a diagnosis.
